clue.text: Kindling picked up after a knock at the nursery door

parts.words: Kindling picked up after a knock at the nursery door
parts.note: surface reading: a child gathers firewood once someone has knocked at the nursery

parts.words: picked up after a knock at the nursery door
parts.note: setter's reading: the counting rhyme 'One, two, buckle my shoe' goes 'three, four, knock at the door; five, six, pick up' these

explanation.surface: Someone gathers kindling after a knock at the nursery door.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is the nursery rhyme 'One, two, buckle my shoe': 'Three, four, knock at the door; Five, six, pick up STICKS.'
explanation.definitionFit: Small dry twigs gathered to light a fire are exactly what people call kindling.

clue.text: Military band

parts.note: surface reading: a regimental band of musicians playing marches
setter's reading: band in its sense of a group of people, here a unit of soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: A band sounds like musicians, but it also means any group of people; a group of soldiers is a TROOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a cavalry or armoured unit of soldiers, so it is a band of fighting men.

clue.text: Many take off and raise tropical headgear to this drink dispenser

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
the word off from the phrase, as in to be off

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a topee is a sun helmet worn in the tropics

explanation.surface: Many people doff their pith helmets in salute to the coffee urn.
explanation.walkthrough: C + OFF + TOPEE written upwards (EEPOT) gives COFFEEPOT. A topee (or topi) is the pith helmet of colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffeepot is a jug from which the brewed beverage is poured, so it dispenses a drink.

clue.text: Swithin's music?

parts.note: surface reading: a tune written by or for someone called Swithin
setter's reading: Saint Swithin, whose feast day on 15 July is said to bring forty days of rain

explanation.walkthrough: St Swithin's Day is the British weather legend that rain on 15 July lasts forty days, so his ST and his RAIN make STRAIN, a word for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage or snatch of melody, as in the strains of a band drifting across a park.

clue.text: Flower of youth mourned by Apollo

parts.words: Flower of youth mourned by Apollo
parts.note: surface reading: the flower of youth, a young person in their prime, grieved over by a god
setter's reading: the Greek myth of a young man whom Apollo loved and accidentally killed with a discus

explanation.surface: Apollo grieves for a beautiful young man cut down in his prime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower of youth' reads as a set phrase, but it splits: Apollo's beloved Hyacinthus died and a flower sprang from his blood, named HYACINTH after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyacinth is a fragrant spring bulb plant with dense spikes of blooms.

clue.text: Conflict of the Century

parts.note: surface reading: the greatest war or fight of the age, a newspaper headline phrase
setter's reading: a century taken literally as a span of a hundred years

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the Century' sounds like hype for a boxing match, but read literally a century is a hundred years, naming the long Anglo-French war of 1337 to 1453.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hundred Years War was the long series of wars between England and France in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: It's chancy having beer with a party-man

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
taken as written
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Drinking beer with a political activist is a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on luck or random outcome, from the Latin for a dice player.

clue.text: 's no place like home, as some northerners might say?

parts.words: 's no place like home, as some northerners might say?
parts.note: surface reading: the familiar saying 'There's no place like home', with its opening word missing
setter's reading: Inuit of the Arctic, who would fill the gap with the name of their snow-block dwelling

explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts mid-sentence: the blank before 's is the answer, so the Arctic version of the saying runs 'IGLOO's no place like home'.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a domed shelter built from blocks of snow, the traditional dwelling of Arctic peoples.

clue.text: Tree-lined carriage-way ?

parts.note: surface reading: an avenue with trees planted along both sides
setter's reading: led by the main stem of a tree, which comes first in the name of the road

explanation.walkthrough: The tree part is the trunk, and the carriageway is the road: a TRUNK ROAD is a major British highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk road is a main route for long-distance traffic, a principal carriageway between cities.

clue.text: Meeting to discuss a type of pear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a formal gathering for talks
second meaning: a long green English dessert pear variety

explanation.surface: Someone calls a meeting to debate which pear variety to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A conference is a formal discussion meeting, and Conference is also a popular British pear cultivar.

clue.text: Double back and celebrate

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: Someone retraces their steps and then throws a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud someone is to praise and glorify them, which is to celebrate them.

clue.text: Better progress implied by less haste…

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the phrase describes the quality it names

parts.words: Better progress implied by less haste
parts.note: surface reading: going slower makes you get on better
setter's reading: the proverb 'more haste, less speed', turned round so that less haste means more speed

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says more haste, less speed; flip it and less haste implies more speed, so SPEEDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedier means quicker, making faster headway than before.

clue.text: … or kit move with a three horse-power vehicle

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them about, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shifts their gear into a carriage pulled by three horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link this clue to the one before. 'Three horse-power' plays on an engine's rating but means literally three horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sledge drawn by a team of three horses abreast.

clue.text: Cheeky fellow

parts.note: surface reading: an impudent man
setter's reading: to do with the cheek, since the word also means a jaw or cheek

explanation.walkthrough: Cheeky suggests insolence, but chap (often chops) also means the jaw or cheek, so this fellow is cheeky by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British English for a man or bloke.

clue.text: Handy cure prepared to get everyone on the run

definitions.note: the phrase names a noisy public pursuit, which sets everyone running

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A convenient remedy has been made ready to get people back on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Under old English law, the hue and cry was the shout that obliged everyone who heard it to chase a fleeing criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue and cry is a public outcry and chase after a wrongdoer, with the whole neighbourhood pursuing.

clue.text: Did Othello return by night here to await developments ?

parts.note: night is the dark

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for Othello runs the other way

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Did Othello come back under cover of night to wait for what happened next?
explanation.walkthrough: DARK + MOOR written backwards (ROOM). 'Developments' sounds like plot twists, but it means photographic film being developed.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom is a lightless room where photographers process film, waiting for images to develop.

clue.text: Balance to hand over about May, in France

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to render is to give or hand over, as in render payment
mai is the French name for the month of May

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pay the outstanding sum by May, in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' tells you to use the French word for the month, not the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance is what is left over after deductions, which is the remainder.

clue.text: Had in mind a fiance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: planned or meant to do
second meaning: the person one is engaged to marry

explanation.definitionFit: Intended is a past-tense verb for meant or planned, and also an old-fashioned noun for one's future spouse.

clue.text: No more than fine words, the miscreant hopes?

parts.words: No more than fine words, the miscreant hopes?
parts.note: surface reading: a wrongdoer hopes to get off with mere talk
setter's reading: the offender in court hopes the punishment handed down will be only a monetary penalty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine words' looks like eloquence, but it splits: the miscreant hopes the judge's ruling will be no more than a fine, and the answer is also a string of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is both a grammatical group of words and the punishment a court imposes.

clue.text: With this fashion the Navy's up-to-date

parts.words: With this fashion the Navy's up-to-date
parts.note: surface reading: the navy has adopted the latest style
setter's reading: add this word to the abbreviation for the Royal Navy and the result means current

explanation.walkthrough: The Navy is RN, the Royal Navy; put MODE before it and you get MODERN, up-to-date.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a prevailing style or trend, as in the latest mode in clothing.

clue.text: Work one devoured, as a sleep-inducer

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a musical work
I is the Roman numeral one
ate means devoured

explanation.surface: Someone works, eats a big meal and falls asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, used to dull pain and bring on drowsiness.

clue.text: Natural to twist at nine

indicators.note: to twist something is to bend it out of shape, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It comes naturally to dance the twist at nine o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn rather than learned, so they come naturally.

clue.text: Friend of Mowgli in the Lakelands

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the next words, waiting to be found

parts.note: found inside the second word

explanation.surface: A friend of the jungle boy Mowgli turns up in the English Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Mowgli is the boy raised by wolves in Kipling's The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the wise old wolf who leads the pack and protects Mowgli in Kipling's Jungle Book.

clue.text: Suspension of suspension perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a pause in a pause, an odd repetition
setter's reading: suspension as hanging from the gallows, which a condemned person may have postponed

explanation.walkthrough: The second suspension means hanging; calling off or postponing an execution is a REPRIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a cancellation or postponement of punishment, especially a death sentence.

clue.text: Guarantee a vanadium brooch

parts.note: V is the chemical symbol for vanadium
ouch is an archaic word for a clasp or brooch set with jewels

explanation.surface: Someone guarantees that a brooch is made of a rare metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch is to give an assurance or personal guarantee for someone or something.

clue.text: A back-door, that's the fourth in this area

parts.words: A back-door, that's the fourth in this area
parts.note: surface reading: a rear door counted as the fourth one in some district
setter's reading: the word door read from back to front gives an old unit of land equal to a quarter of the answer

explanation.walkthrough: DOOR backwards is ROOD, an old British land measure, and four roods make one ACRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards, traditionally divided into four roods.

clue.text: Unfortunate state of the poor pugilist

definitions.note: the answer describes the pugilist rather than naming one
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a boxer floored and then counted out

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer knocked down and counted out is literally down and out.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-and-out means penniless and without prospects, and literally describes a boxer floored and out of the fight.

clue.text: Some talk of a Spartan hero

parts.words: Some talk of a Spartan hero
parts.note: surface reading: people discussing a brave warrior from ancient Sparta
setter's reading: the opening of the song The British Grenadiers, 'Some talk of Alexander', with a rhyming name swapped in

explanation.walkthrough: The British Grenadiers begins 'Some talk of Alexander'; the Spartan whose name rhymes is LYSANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysander was the Spartan admiral who defeated Athens at Aegospotami and ended the Peloponnesian War.

clue.text: Terribly hearty like our homely space traveller ?

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Our cosy spaceship crew are very cheerful indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The homely space traveller is our home planet, which carries us through space; something like it is EARTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy means resembling soil or the ground, the stuff our planet is made of, and also unrefined and down to earth.
